questions.q: What is the main goal of a user interview in early product discovery?
options: Understand people's needs, habits and pain points
Get users to approve the final design
Convince the user to buy the product
Collect bug reports from the live app

questions.q: A persona in UX work is best described as:
options: A list of the app's main features
A research-based profile of a typical user group
The brand's mascot character
A real customer chosen for testimonials

questions.q: Which method best shows how people naturally group the items in your app's menu?
options: A/B testing
A heatmap of the home page
Card sorting
A Net Promoter Score survey

questions.q: Your PM wants to build a feature because two app-store reviews asked for it. What do you do first?
options: Start high-fidelity mockups right away so the team can see it early
Reject it, since two reviews mean nothing
Ship it in the next release as a hidden setting
Check how many users face the underlying problem, using data and a few interviews

questions.q: In a journey map for booking an LPG cylinder refill, what do the pain points show?
options: Moments where the user feels friction or frustration
Screens with the most traffic
Steps that earn the company money
Places where banner ads can be added

questions.q: Why should you avoid asking "Would you use this feature?" in user interviews?
options: It takes too long for users to answer
People predict their future behaviour poorly; ask about past actions instead
It is not allowed under data protection rules
It can reveal the product roadmap to competitors who join as participants

questions.q: Interviewees in Bengaluru say they love your grocery app's new filters, but analytics show few people use them. Best next step?
options: Trust the interviews, since users said so directly
Remove the filters in the next release
Watch users do real shopping tasks to see where the filters get missed
Send a push notification about filters to every user

questions.q: For a crop-advisory app used by farmers in rural Maharashtra, which research approach gives the most reliable insight?
options: An English online survey shared on LinkedIn
Lab sessions with office staff in Pune
Reading competitor app reviews only

questions.q: Which of these is qualitative research data?
options: Quotes and observations from user interviews
Daily active user count
Conversion rate from analytics
Average order value in ₹

questions.q: What is a wireframe?
options: The final coloured design handed to developers
A low-detail layout showing structure and where content goes
The app's database schema
A recorded video of a user test

questions.q: Why show a clear progress state while a UPI payment is processing?
options: To make the app look more modern
To show an ad while the payment runs
So users know it is working and don't tap pay again
To slow users down so they read the terms

questions.q: Hick's law suggests that:
options: Bigger targets are always faster to tap
Users read pages in an F pattern
Seven items is the hard limit for a menu
More choices increase the time needed to decide

questions.q: On a mobile checkout, where should the main "Pay ₹499" button usually sit?
options: Near the bottom within thumb reach, visually dominant
At the top right next to the logo
Inside an overflow menu
Below the full terms and conditions text

questions.q: Users of a delivery app often delete the wrong saved address. Which change helps most?
options: Show an "Are you sure?" popup on every action
Offer an undo option for a few seconds after deleting
Remove the delete feature entirely
Make the delete icon smaller and grey

questions.q: What does progressive disclosure mean?
options: Revealing the final price only at the last step
Loading images slowly as the user scrolls
Showing advanced options only when the user needs them
Releasing features to users in stages

questions.q: A KYC form has 18 fields on one screen and 60% of users drop off. Which redesign is most likely to help?
options: Shrink the fields so all of them fit above the fold
Add a progress bar but keep the single screen
Move all help text into tooltips on each field
Split into short steps, prefill known data, ask only what is needed now

questions.q: When should a form check a field like a PAN number and show an error?
options: When the user leaves the field, saying exactly what to fix
Only after the whole form is submitted
On every keystroke from the first character
Never; let the backend reject it

questions.q: Your design system has two button styles that look almost the same but trigger very different actions. Main risk?
options: The app's file size grows a lot with every extra variant
Users can't predict the outcome, which causes errors and distrust
Developers need more colour tokens
It breaks the brand's logo guidelines

questions.q: What does visual hierarchy help users do?
options: Load the page faster
Print the page correctly
See what matters most first
Translate text automatically

questions.q: Why use a consistent spacing scale such as 4, 8, 16 and 24 px?
options: It makes images load faster
It is needed for search ranking
It lets users change their font size
It keeps layouts tidy and predictable across screens

questions.q: Which file format suits icons that must stay sharp at any size?
options: SVG
JPG
GIF
BMP

questions.q: For long reading text on mobile, a comfortable body style is usually around:
options: 10 px with tight line height
16 px with about 1.5 line height
24 px bold for every paragraph
12 px in all capitals

questions.q: Your app shows labels in English, Hindi and Tamil. What should the layout allow for?
options: Fixed-width buttons sized to fit the English labels
All text set in one Latin-only font
Flexible widths, since translated text can be longer or taller
Labels cut with an ellipsis everywhere

questions.q: Using the same red for error messages and the main "Buy now" button can cause what issue?
options: The screen uses more battery
Developers can't export the colour
It breaks the grid layout
Users may read the main action as a warning

questions.q: A stakeholder wants the logo three times bigger and every section highlighted. How do you respond?
options: Show options tied to the business goal, explaining how heavy emphasis hides key actions
Do exactly as told, since the stakeholder approves the final work
Refuse and escalate to their manager
Make the change now and quietly reduce it next build

questions.q: Why use design tokens (named values for colour, spacing and type)?
options: They compress images for faster loading
One change updates every use consistently in design and code
They remove the need for any style guide
They let users pick any theme with no code at all

questions.q: In dark mode, why avoid pure white text on a pure black background?
options: Pure black is not allowed on Android
Pure black drains more battery than dark grey on OLED screens
The extreme contrast causes glare and smearing; softer tones read better
White text can't be anti-aliased on black

questions.q: What minimum contrast ratio does WCAG AA require for normal body text?
Why add alt text to an image?
options: Screen readers can describe it to people who can't see it
It improves the image's colour quality
It stops others from copying the image
It makes the image load first

questions.q: Which practice causes problems for colour-blind users?
options: Adding an icon and message beside the error
Showing an error only by turning the field red
Putting text labels on chart lines
Underlining links in body text

questions.q: A common minimum size for touch targets on mobile is roughly:
options: 16 px square
24 px wide by 12 px tall
44 to 48 px square
100 px square

questions.q: What should happen when a keyboard user tabs through a form?
options: Focus jumps to the footer first
The outline is hidden for a cleaner look
Only the submit button can take focus
Focus moves in a logical order with a visible outline

questions.q: An elderly user can't read the OTP screen because the text is tiny and fixed. Best fix?
options: Support system font scaling so text grows with phone settings
Add a zoom button only on the OTP screen
Auto-fill the OTP and hide the text
Switch to a thinner, more elegant font

questions.q: Your custom dropdown is built from plain divs. What must it have for screen reader users?
options: A larger font size
Proper roles, states and keyboard support, or use a native select
A tooltip that describes the dropdown
A brighter background colour

questions.q: A government-scheme app must be accessible but the deadline is close. What do you prioritise?
options: Build a separate "accessible version" page later
Run an automated checker and treat a pass as done
Fix blockers on key flows first: keyboard access, labels and contrast
Add an accessibility statement to the footer

questions.q: Why is an automated accessibility scanner not enough on its own?
options: It only works on English websites and fails on Indian languages
It slows down the live website
It changes your code without asking
It misses issues needing judgement, like confusing order or poor alt text

questions.q: In a usability test, what should the moderator mostly do?
options: Give tasks, observe, and avoid leading the user
Explain how each screen works
Help the user whenever they pause
Defend the design when users struggle

questions.q: What does an A/B test compare?
options: Two designers' opinions on one screen, collected in a review meeting
Two versions shown to different users to see which performs better
The Android and iOS versions of the app
The old and new logo in a survey

questions.q: During a test, a participant asks, "Should I tap here?" What do you say?
options: "Yes, that's the right button."
"No, try the other one."
"What would you expect to happen if you did?"
"Let me show you how it works."

questions.q: In a small qualitative usability round, about how many users often reveal most major issues?
Which metric best shows whether users can complete "add a new payee"?
options: Task success rate
App store rating
Number of screens in the flow
Page views per session

questions.q: After a redesign, checkout conversion rose but support calls about wrong orders doubled. What do you conclude?
options: The redesign succeeded and the calls are unrelated
The change may make mistakes easier; investigate before calling it a win
Roll back at once without looking further
Conversion is the only number that matters

questions.q: Your A/B test shows version B ahead after 2 days with 80 users. What is the right call?
options: Ship B now since it is winning
Stop the test and keep A, because changing is a risk
Keep running until the planned sample size and duration are reached
Restart with a new version C

questions.q: Five of six test users missed the "Apply coupon" link, but the PM says it is fine. How do you make the case?
options: Insist, as the UX expert, that it must change
Drop it to avoid conflict
Retest with users who already know the app well, to confirm

questions.q: What is the main weakness of relying only on a System Usability Scale (SUS) score?
options: It shows how usable the product feels, not which problems to fix
It can only be used for websites
It needs at least 1,000 responses

task.title: Review a rent-payment screen and write a prioritised UX fix list
task.brief: Read the description of a 'Pay rent' screen in a payments app (below). In about 25 minutes, write a short UX review for the product team. List the 5 most important problems you see. For each one say: what the problem is, who it hurts and why (refer to usability or accessibility principles), your suggested fix, and a priority (high / medium / low). End with 2–3 lines on how you would check your fixes work with real users before full release. A good answer is specific to this screen, puts the problems that cause payment mistakes or drop-off first, and is easy for a PM and developer to act on.
task.material:
PAY RENT screen (Android app, used across India, many first-time digital payers)

- Header: small grey text 'Rent' (12 px) on a light grey background.
- Field 1: 'Landlord UPI ID' (free text). No check that the ID exists; the landlord's name is not shown before paying.
- Field 2: 'Amount' with no ₹ sign; users can type 25000 or 2,50,00 and both are accepted.
- Field 3: 'Month' dropdown, defaults to January every time.
- A 'Use rewards' toggle and a 'Add GST invoice' toggle sit above the amount, both ON by default.
- Fee: a convenience fee of ₹249 appears only on the next screen.
- Two buttons at the bottom side by side, same size and same blue colour: 'Cancel' (left) and 'Pay' (right).
- Errors: if anything is wrong, the whole form clears and a red toast says 'Error 4012' for 2 seconds.
- The screen is English only; the app elsewhere supports Hindi and Telugu.
- Text does not grow when the phone's font size setting is increased.
- Analytics: 41% of users who open the screen leave without paying; support gets ~300 tickets a week for 'paid wrong person'.
key_points: Flags paying the wrong person: verify the UPI ID and show the payee's name before payment
Flags the hidden ₹249 fee and asks for total cost to be shown up front
Flags error handling: form clearing and a meaningless code; keep input and give a clear fix message
Flags Cancel and Pay looking identical side by side; make Pay the clear primary action
Mentions amount formatting/validation (₹ sign, Indian digit grouping) and smart month default
Mentions accessibility: low contrast, tiny text, no font scaling, and missing Hindi/Telugu
Questions toggles that are ON by default (rewards, GST) as unclear or dark-pattern-like
Prioritises by impact on payment mistakes and drop-off, using the analytics given
Proposes a validation plan: usability test with target users and/or an A/B test with clear metrics

rubric.label: Finds the real problems
rubric.guide: 0 = misses the main issues or lists only cosmetic ones, 3 = finds some key issues, 5 = finds the wrong-payee, hidden fee and error-handling issues plus others

rubric.label: Explains why
rubric.guide: 0 = no reasons, 3 = some reasons but generic, 5 = each problem tied to users, principles or the analytics

rubric.label: Quality of fixes
rubric.guide: 0 = vague or no fixes, 3 = workable fixes for some, 5 = specific, practical fixes a developer could build

rubric.label: Prioritisation and validation
rubric.guide: 0 = no priorities or test plan, 3 = priorities given but weakly justified, 5 = clear impact-based priorities and a sensible way to test

rubric.label: Clarity
rubric.guide: 0 = hard to follow, 3 = understandable but wordy, 5 = short, structured and easy for a PM to act on
